author: Codex documentation author; corrections by DOC-029 source-review author agent (admin-org)

prerequisites: Owned unseeded scenario-fixture lab openlaw-docs-41255c61-adminorg-auth built from 3fa407e3 with Mailpit, a local OpenID Connect fixture (oauth2-mock-server 9.2.0) on the lab network, and the first Administrator created through /auth/setup.
Fictional staff and Business User accounts named doc029-auth-*; allowed domain northwind.example.
scenarios.expected: Allowed users can sign in and test mail reaches the controlled sink through the active configuration source. Invalid issuer/relay, denied domain, and locked environment settings have recoverable outcomes without exposing secrets.
scenarios.actual: 34 recorded steps passed on 3fa407e3 for the Administrator, Legal Team Member and Business User identities in the owned unseeded lab. First-run: Skip optional steps on Welcome opened Outbound email, which had no Set up later and a disabled Continue. An http:// relay URL was refused with "The relay URL must start with smtp:// or smtps://." Save relay showed "Relay saved.", never displayed the URL, and Send test email delivered to the signed-in Administrator from the stored From address. A saved unreachable relay failed its test ("The test email could not be sent. The relay host could not be found...") until Replace relay fixed it. Clear relay showed "Relay cleared. This instance can no longer send email.", disabled Continue and stopped mail until a replacement was saved. After Finish, /welcome redirected to / and Settings had no email page. Settings, Security, Authentication showed Legal User Authentication and Business Portal Authentication, each with Email and password, Email magic link, Single sign-on (SSO) and Require two-factor authentication; SSO was unavailable before registration. Turning off the last method showed "Enable at least one sign-in method." With Legal password sign-in off, the Administrator still signed in with a password and a Legal Team Member was refused, including on the Portal page; a Business User signed in with a password on the staff page. Existing staff on non-allowed domains got magic links, and an invited row stayed Invited after one. An allowed northwind.example entrant got a link and became a Business User; an unapproved address got no link and no password setup link. After Remove northwind.example: no new link for the existing Business User, but its held session, an earlier unused link and its password sign-in still worked; a password setup link issued earlier failed at completion with "Password setup is no longer available for this address."; a never-seen address's earlier link gave no session and no account; staff still got links. Turning off Email magic link for the Portal made an earlier link fail and removed the magic-link choice. An unreachable issuer was refused. Registering http://oidc:8080 showed the callback http://127.0.0.1:23310/api/auth/sso/callback, turned on no group, and fixed the Provider ID. With SSO on for Legal users, an invited staff account signed in through the fixture, kept Legal team member, and became Active; an uninvited identity got no account. Save provider with a blank secret and with a new secret both kept sign-in working; an unreachable issuer update was refused and the provider kept working. With Portal SSO on, an existing Business User on the provider domain signed in, and still could after that domain was removed, while a new identity on it was refused. Recovery with only SSO on for Legal users: the Administrator signed in with a password, then turned password on and SSO off. With Require two-factor authentication on, an Administrator and a Legal Team Member (after a magic-link sign-in) were sent to enrolment with "Your organization requires two-factor authentication." and API calls were refused; a new session asked for a code; turning the switch on as an Administrator without an authenticator went straight to enrolment.

prerequisites: The same owned lab with its unfinished welcome wizard and a complete stored relay.
Hashed Compose overlays applied by phase.sh to the owned project only.
scenarios.expected: Allowed users can sign in and test mail reaches the controlled sink through the active configuration source. Invalid issuer/relay, denied domain, and locked environment settings have recoverable outcomes without exposing secrets.
scenarios.actual: 3 recorded steps passed on 3fa407e3. Operator responsibility was performed with deployment tools on the owned lab, not through an app role. Each phase recreated only the owned app and worker with a hashed overlay, recorded in walkthrough-r1.json. Phase env (overlay-phase-env.json sha256 23eb5607...) set SMTP_URL and SMTP_FROM while a complete stored relay existed: Outbound email read "Outbound email is set by the deployment environment. Mail is sent from DOC-029 Environment <env-relay@helix.example>." with no Save relay, Replace relay, Clear relay or Send test email, a direct save answered 409, and an invitation from Invite your team arrived from env-relay@helix.example rather than the stored sender. Phase incomplete (overlay-phase-incomplete.json sha256 fa2209f8...) set SMTP_URL without SMTP_FROM: the step warned "The deployment environment sets SMTP_URL but not SMTP_FROM, so mail cannot be sent.", the source was env with no from address, Continue was disabled, and an invitation the Users API accepted (201) produced no message. Removing the override (overlay-phase-stored.json sha256 98d274e9...) and recreating app and worker returned "Outbound email is set in the app. Mail is sent from DOC-029 Stored <stored-relay@helix.example>." and a delivered test message from the stored sender.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and the source reviewer; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.

Single sign-on was verified against a local OpenID Connect fixture with real discovery, authorize, token, JWKS and userinfo endpoints and the real OpenLaw callback. It is not certification of a real provider. The fixture accepts any client secret, so secret retention and rotation were checked as successful saves followed by working sign-ins, not as proof of which secret is stored.

Single sign-on links or creates accounts only for emails on the provider's Email domain. Portal single sign-on was therefore checked with a Business User on the provider domain; a first attempt with a northwind.example Business User failed for that reason and is kept in runs/superseded.
Require two-factor authentication was checked with password and email magic-link sign-ins, not with single sign-on.

lab.mjs up could not create the lab networks because the host's Docker address pools were exhausted by other projects. The same images ran through phase.sh with explicit subnets (overlay-networks.json). The lab source/.env and overlay.json were not modified, and the app and engine image IDs match the shared admin lab.

The dev worktree text of this article was verified. Another session edits the same article in the main checkout; that text was not verified. The lab Help route serves the article bytes committed at 3fa407e3, and Help discovery was not checked.
Some runs had reviewer script faults; they and their dispositions are kept in walkthrough-r1.json and runs/superseded. Every observation cited here passed in a retained run.
